state.misconception_label: Confuses rest and movement on a distance time graph

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I have: This graph shows how far Fido the dog is from his home. What might the negative-sloping section represent? ![A graph with time (secs) on the horizontal axis and distance (m) on the vertical axis. The graph starts at the origin, travels in a straight line up and right, travels horizontally, then travels in a straight line down and right back to the x-axis. ](). I got Fido has fallen asleep because I'm not sure I worked it out the right way.

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think Fido falling asleep would correspond to the negative-sloping section on the graph? How does the movement on the graph relate to Fido's distance from home?

turn_history.speaker: student
turn_history.text: I thought that if Fido was asleep, he wouldn't be moving, so the line going down meant he was just staying still or something. But now I'm not sure if that makes sense because the line is going down, which might mean he's getting closer to home? Can you explain how the negative slope really shows movement instead of just resting?

turn_history.speaker: teacher
turn_history.text: Why do you think the negative slope might indicate movement rather than rest? How does the direction of the line on the graph relate to Fido's distance from home?
